newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-W.Australia looks for first Ord cotton in '97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-W.Australia looks for first Ord cotton in '97.

text.p: Western Australia was expected to produce its first cotton from the revitalised Ord River irrigation project in November/December 1997, a spokesman for state Prime Industry Minister Monty House said on Monday.
This would follow successful cotton trials in 1996, he said.

The establishment of a viable state cotton industry looked promising following results from the state's first transgenic cotton harvest in the Ord district of the Kimberley region in the state's northwest, House said in a statement.
Commercially acceptable yields and fibre quality, comparable with eastern state yields, had been recorded over trial production from 50 hectares (ha) in 1996, he said.
The trial area would be increased to 250 ha in 1997 when first production of cotton was expected to begin, he said.
The spokesman for House said that cotton from the 50 ha trial area was not processed but processing was planned to begin in 1997 after construction of Colly Cotton Ltd's new A$800,000 gin.
At budgeted yields of eight bales a ha, the 250 ha was expected to produce between 1,600 and 2,000 500-pound bales, he said.
This would suggest that a commercial cotton industry could be established in the Ord, he said.
Yields over three years of trials, between 1994 and 1996, averaged between 9.5 and 10.0 bales a ha, he said.
Ord cotton is planted in March/April and picked in September/October.
